authoredCarry.rule: `next` drains evolve/queue/goals.json (authored) before evolve/queue/generated.json, so a re-plan can never starve the authored backlog. `plan` writes generated.json ONLY; goals.json is read-only to it.

considered.title: The DOM gate checks 112 ids from src/ui.js and misses 23 of the 135 ids the app actually references
considered.thesis: dom=1.0000 is saturated, but the gate derives its id set from ONE regex over src/ui.js: /\$\("([^"]+)"\)/g. Scanning every src/**/*.js for $("id"), getElementById("id") and querySelector("#id") finds 135 distinct ids, of which 23 are never checked: ligandLegend, settingsModal, settingsBtn, networkCanvas, networkInfo, netStepBtn, netMultiStepBtn, netMasterEqBtn, .... A typo in any of those 23 ids is invisible to the gate AND to scripts/wikiskill_gate.js, so dom=1.0 reports coverage the project does not have.
considered.acceptance: The dom component of the gate (and scripts/wikiskill_gate.js) is derived from a full scan of src/**/*.js, not src/ui.js alone; every one of the 135 referenced ids is checked against index.html. A test plants a bad id in a non-ui.js module and asserts the gate catches it.

considered.title: coverage=1.0000 is saturated by counting only tests/test_*.js — 9 scripts/ validators are outside the denominator
considered.thesis: countTests() globs the tests/ directory for /^test_.*\.js$/ and finds 51, all wired, so coverage = (51+0)/51 = 1.0 and is reported saturated. The scripts/ directory holds 9 more test-bearing files (scripts/test_bindlog.mjs, scripts/test_bindlog_integration.mjs, scripts/test_bindviz.mjs, scripts/test_pocket_entropy.mjs, scripts/test_thermo.mjs, scripts/test_thermo_heavy.mjs, scripts/validate_1crn_null.mjs, scripts/validate_binding_physics_r1.mjs, scripts/validate_flexlig.mjs) that no component counts. One of them, scripts/validate_binding_physics_r1.mjs, currently exits 1 — the gate is saturated on a population that excludes the failing member. Measured coverage of the real population is 51/60 = 85.0%, not 100%.
considered.acceptance: The coverage component counts every test-bearing file (tests/test_*.js AND scripts/{test,validate}_*.mjs not in tests/manual/), and the number it reports equals (wired+manual)/total over that full population. A validator moved into scripts/ can change the score.

considered.title: 3 of 612 `file:line` citations across 68 markdown files point at nothing
considered.thesis: Measured by resolving every `name.ext:NN` citation in every tracked *.md against the working tree: 612 citations checked, 3 unresolvable — TRANSFORMATION_PLAN_100.md:177 -> src/viewer-gl.js:19 (no such file); docs/BINDING_LOOP2_DONE.md:842 -> wikiskill/README.md:24 (no such file); docs/CITATION.md:53 -> .wikiskill/README.md:59 (file has 41 lines). These are the load-bearing sentences of the project's validation record ("all §0 code claims machine-verified"), and one of the failures is a citation to a file that a previous evolution DELETED, so the record now describes code that does not exist. A claim that cannot be resolved is a claim nobody can check, and a doc that is wrong about the code is worse than a doc that is silent.
considered.acceptance: Every `file:line` citation in tracked *.md resolves to an existing file with at least that many lines. The check runs as a test in the FAST tier (or tests/manual/ with a README entry), so drift fails a gate rather than being found by a reader.

considered.title: Cut src LOC below the bloat knee: 23235 LOC vs the 20000 penalty start
considered.thesis: bloat=0.9341 is the only non-saturated gate component (everything else is pinned at 1.0), and 52.8% of its remaining headroom is the src-LOC term 1/(1+(L-20000)/20000) evaluated at L=23235. dR/dL = -0.093 per 100 LOC at this point, so the loop currently pays a measurable price for every line of science code it writes — an incentive pointing the wrong way. Cutting L to 20000 recovers 0.0348 of the 0.0659 deficit.
considered.acceptance: src LOC (sum of lines over src/**/*.js as counted by evolve.mjs readTrackedStats) <= 20000, or the bloat LOC term is replaced by a term with an argued-for justification. `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` reports bloat >= 0.9689.

considered.title: Eliminate the tracked files >1MB that hold the bloat file penalty open: 1 file(s)
considered.thesis: bloat=0.9341; the filePenalty term is 1/(1+bigFiles/20) = 0.9524 with bigFiles = 1: data/pdbbind_parsed.csv 1147KB. Each big file costs ~0.0227 of R, 36.1% of the live deficit. Total tracked is 15.0MB over 297 files, so the size term is nearly satisfied and the penalty is entirely about 1 outlier file(s).
considered.acceptance: Zero tracked files exceed 1MB (evolve.mjs readTrackedStats bigFiles == []) OR each remaining one is a regenerable artifact with a recorded fetch manifest. `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` reports filePenalty == 1.

goals.title: scripts/validate_binding_physics_r1.mjs exits 1 and is wired into NO gate that can fail
goals.thesis: Measured right now: `node scripts/validate_binding_physics_r1.mjs` exits 1 inside the 60s probe budget. Last line: "Node.js v22.23.0". It is NOT registered in tests/suites.js. No CI workflow names it. The gate's coverage component counts only tests/test_*.js, so this file is outside its denominator entirely. A red validator the default gate never runs is indistinguishable from no validator — which is exactly how evolve/reports/test-inventory.md recorded it as a standing finding and left it standing.
goals.acceptance: `node scripts/validate_binding_physics_r1.mjs` exits 0, OR the file is moved to a tier that `npm test`/CI actually executes (justified by its measured runtime). The failing assertion is fixed at its source — not weakened, not deleted. `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` goes red if it regresses again.

goals.title: 56 empty catch blocks in src/ swallow every error they see
goals.thesis: Measured: `grep -rn "catch.*{\s*}" src/` returns 56 empty catch blocks across 9 files — e.g. src/analysis/dccm.js:277, src/analysis/thermo_sasa.js:324, src/analysis-panel.js:164, src/analysis-panel.js:191, src/analysis-panel.js:192, .... A swallowed exception is a failed operation that reports success. A scientist who loads a bad PDB must never see a frozen viewer and conclude the software is broken in an interesting way; right now 56 code paths can produce exactly that. The count is the acceptance criterion, so this is falsifiable: it either goes to 0 or each one is justified in writing.
goals.acceptance: grep finds zero empty catch blocks in src/ (currently 56); every remaining catch either rethrows, logs with the error object, or increments a visible HUD counter. A test feeds a malformed PDB and asserts a specific visible message, and asserts the swallowed-error counter is 0 after a clean load.

goals.title: 109 hardcoded ?v= cache-bust literals across 32 src/ files disagree with src/version.js VERSION "1.1.0-fp7"
goals.thesis: Measured: every ?v= literal in src/**/*.js, counted by value. src/version.js declares VERSION = "1.1.0-fp7", but 109 import specifiers carry a literal ?v= and 1 distinct literal value(s) disagree with it: ?v=10 in 109 files. A module edited without editing this literal is served from the browser cache, and the symptom is "my fix did nothing" — the single most expensive class of bug to diagnose. The version bump is currently not one edit; it is 32 edits that nothing checks.
goals.acceptance: Zero hardcoded ?v= literals remain in src/ (a loader injects the version from src/version.js), OR a check fails when any ?v= disagrees with src/version.js and that check is wired into npm run check and CI. Verified by editing a module, reloading, and observing the change.

goals.title: 6 private fields are ASSIGNED in src/ and never read anywhere: src/capture/bindlog.js this._attached, src/forcefield.js this._seqW, src/physics/network.js this._pmfDerivedBarrier, src/physics/network.js this._pmfScale, src/viewer.js this._amp
goals.thesis: Measured: for every `this._x = ...` in src/**/*.js, count occurrences of `_x` across all of src/. Fields with exactly one occurrence (the assignment) are write-only. Found 6: src/capture/bindlog.js this._attached, src/forcefield.js this._seqW, src/physics/network.js this._pmfDerivedBarrier, src/physics/network.js this._pmfScale, src/viewer.js this._amp, src/viewer.js this._requestClear. Each is a value the code computes and then discards — e.g. a PMF-derived barrier that is stored and never used to rebuild anything, so a function named for an effect has no effect. A reader (or the next agent) sees the assignment and infers the behaviour exists.
goals.acceptance: Every private field assigned in src/ is read at least once, or the assignment is removed. A test enumerates `this._x = ` assignments in src/ and fails on any with zero reads, so the class cannot regrow silently.

goals.title: The gate's only live gradient punishes the work the loop exists to do: dR/dLOC = -0.0009 R per 100 LOC
goals.thesis: Measured: bloat is the only non-saturated component (all others are pinned at 1.0), and its src-LOC term is 1/(1+(L-20000)/20000) with L = 23235. The derivative is dR/dL = -0.25 x 20000/L^2 = -9.262e-6 per LOC, i.e. -0.0009 R per 100 lines. Two consequences, both measured: (1) writing correct code LOWERS R, so a goal that improves the science and adds 500 LOC is scored as a regression; (2) the composite on the CURRENT, UNMODIFIED tree is 0.9341 while R_best is 0.935, so `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` prints "CLOSED (roll back)" for a no-op — the loop is currently in a state where nothing it evaluates can be accepted. An incentive gradient that points away from the loop's purpose is worse than no gradient, because it is trusted.
goals.acceptance: The composite is monotonically non-decreasing in work that improves the project: a change that raises any other component and adds LOC does not lower R. Demonstrated by a test that evaluates the score function at srcLoc and srcLoc+1000 with all other components held fixed and asserts score(L+1000) >= score(L); OR by replacing the LOC term with a justified one and re-baselining R_best with an updated rBaselineNote.

goals.title: src/main.js is 1686 LOC against a src/ median of 279 — 6.0x the typical module
goals.thesis: Measured: line counts of every src/**/*.js. Largest is src/main.js 1686, src/heavy.js 1659, src/forcefield.js 942; median is 279 LOC. src/main.js at 1686 LOC is 6.0x the median and is a single point of syntactic failure: the project's own AUDIT_REPORT.md §1.1 names the god-module failure mode, and one unparseable line inside it takes down every importer. Split by responsibility so the failure domain shrinks.
goals.acceptance: src/main.js is under 400 LOC of pure wiring, its responsibilities live in >= 4 extracted modules that are each independently node --check-able, no behaviour changes (test count >= the pre-split high-water mark), and the DOM contract test still passes. Documented in the README project layout.

goals.title: The gate reports a regression and still exits 0: score 0.9341 < R_best 0.935
goals.thesis: Measured: `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` printed verdict "CLOSED (roll back)" at score 0.9341 against R_best 0.935, and `echo $?` was 0. .github/workflows/check.yml runs the gate as a build step, so a step that can only ever pass gates nothing: the loop's own "reject" signal is discarded by the shell. A gate that cannot fail is not a gate.
goals.acceptance: node evolve/evolve.mjs gate exits non-zero when score < R_best and 0 when score >= R_best; a planted regression makes the CI step red. Proven by a test that sets R_best above the current score and asserts a non-zero exit.

goals.title: bench/budget.json claims heavy_compute_ms 2; measured 14.437 ms/compute (7.2x over)
goals.thesis: Measured: `node bench/perf.js` reports Heavy 14.437 ms/compute on 4w52.pdb (n=1308, 20 warmup + 30 timed). bench/budget.json declares heavy_compute_ms 2. The budget is 7.22x tighter than reality and has been for long enough that docs/PERFORMANCE.md and .github/workflows/check.yml both cite it as the performance contract while CI emits only a ::warning on a permanent 7.2x overrun. A budget nobody believes is worse than no budget: it makes the number meaningless. Either the code gets 7.2x faster or the number becomes the measured one.
goals.acceptance: bench/budget.json heavy_compute_ms is within 1.2x of `node bench/perf.js` output on 4w52.pdb, and docs/PERFORMANCE.md + .github/workflows/check.yml quote the same value. If the physics cannot be made to fit, the budget is rebaselined to the measured p95 with a written justification and the CI step becomes a warn-on-regression-from-baseline rather than a permanent ignore.

goals.title: Give the gate a live gradient: 5/6 components are saturated
goals.thesis: gate vector = {"syntax":1,"testPass":1,"coverage":1,"dom":1,"bloat":0.934107,"science":1}; saturated = [testPass, syntax, dom, science, coverage]; only [bloat] still carries gradient. Weights are renormalised over non-saturated components (evolve.mjs:SAT=0.999), so R is currently a function of 1 number(s) alone. A goal that moves any saturated component scores exactly 0 change, so the loop cannot tell "improved" from "unchanged" on 5 of 6 axes. Measured cost: the R_best-vs-current gap is 0.0009 and 0 of 5 saturated components can close it.
goals.acceptance: A new discriminating component exists with measured spread across the repo (report min/median/max over >= 5 real samples) and it appears unsaturated in `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` output; OR the saturated components are replaced by metrics that provably move. `node evolve/evolve.mjs gate` shows saturated.length <= 4.

goals.title: science=1.0000 is saturated, but the overclaim check reads only 4000 of README.md's 22143 chars and passes on a keyword regex
goals.thesis: scienceScore() computes have/must for 7 files, then multiplies by (overclaim ? 1 : 0.5) where overclaim = /NOT a replacement|qualitative|not FEP|trust boundary/i.test(README.md.slice(0,4000)). Measured: README.md is 22143 chars, so 18143 chars (81.9%) of the project's honest-scope surface is never examined, and the check that IS run is satisfied by a single matching phrase rather than by the absence of an overclaim. Deleting the phrase halves the component; writing a false claim anywhere past char 4000 changes nothing.
goals.acceptance: The overclaim check examines 100% of README.md (and the docs it summarises) and asserts the ABSENCE of specific overclaim patterns rather than the presence of a disclaimer phrase. A test plants a known overclaim sentence and asserts science < 1.0.

goals.title: 2 docs/ files exceed 400 LOC (largest docs/BINDING_LOOP2_DONE.md at 1326 LOC, 1746 LOC combined)
goals.thesis: Measured: line counts of every docs/**/*.md. Over 400 LOC: docs/BINDING_LOOP2_DONE.md 1326, docs/BINDING_PHYSICS_R2.md 420 — 1746 LOC in 2 files. A running log of what was done is not a document a scientist can consult: ROADMAP.md §1 makes the out-of-scope contract the most important document in the repo, and it competes for attention with a 1326-line completion log. Split the log from the guidance so the guidance is findable.
goals.acceptance: Each over-400-LOC doc/ file is split into a durable reference and a dated log (or the log moves to a clearly-named history/ location linked from docs/README.md); docs/README.md still links every file exactly once (tests/test_docs_index.js green) and the ROADMAP/LIMITATIONS/APPLICABILITY/VALIDATION trust-boundary docs remain the first thing listed.

goals.title: bench/budget.json declares fps 30; no file under bench/ or scripts/ measures frame rate at all
goals.thesis: budget.json carries three keys: heavy_compute_ms, cg_compute_ms, fps 30. Measured: `grep -n fps bench/*.js scripts/*.mjs tests/*.js` returns ZERO hits — bench/perf.js measures ms/compute and nothing measures frames. .github/workflows/check.yml prints "fps budget 30 — check render fps via bench/perf.js scale if applicable" and manuscript/reproduce.sh does the same: both reference a measurement that does not exist. One third of the declared performance contract is unfalsifiable.
goals.acceptance: Either a real fps measurement exists (a bench that reports frames/second over a fixed workload, printing a number CI can compare) or the fps key is removed from bench/budget.json and from every doc/script that quotes it. `grep -rn "budget[.fps.]\|budget.get(.fps.)" bench/ scripts/ manuscript/ .github/` returns no unbacked reference.

goals.title: 8 declared constants (SCREAMING_CASE = number) are defined in more than one src/ file
goals.thesis: Measured: every `NAME = <number>` literal in src/**/*.js, indexed by name and value. 8 appear in >= 2 files: SASA=0 in src/analysis/thermo_sasa.js+src/analysis/thermodynamics.js+src/analysis-panel.js; COULOMB_CONST=332.06371 in src/compute/webgpu_backend.js+src/physics/gb.js+src/physics/solvation/gb_obc2.js+src/physics/solvation/membrane_slab.js; BOND_SLACK=1.15 in src/ff-params.js+src/heavy.js+src/pdb.js; R_CUT=8.5 in src/force-worker.js+src/gpu.js+src/heavy.js; RMIN=2.6 in src/forcefield.js+src/physics/integrators/respa.js; STANDARD_VOLUME=1660.54 in src/funnel.js+src/units.js; .... A duplicated physical constant means the CG path and the heavy path can disagree about the same quantity — the class of defect docs/BINDING_PHYSICS_R* spent seven review rounds finding, one of which (KB_KCAL defined twice) was a real 5.03e-8 divergence caught only because a parity test happened to exist. Each duplicate is a future divergence waiting for someone to edit one side.
goals.acceptance: Every duplicated declared constant is defined in exactly one module and imported by the others, and a parity test asserts CG and heavy agree to < 1e-12 for each one. The duplication scan itself becomes a test so the class cannot regrow.

goals.title: 2 of 38 TODO/stub/placeholder hits in src/ are on lines that EXECUTE, not in comments
goals.thesis: Measured by classify-each-hit: `grep -rn "TODO|FIXME|not yet|placeholder|stub" src/` returns 38 hits across 14 files. 36 are comment/leading-* lines — honest scope notes, which ROADMAP.md §1 makes a virtue and which must be left alone. 2 are on lines that execute: src/funnel.js:428, src/mmcif.js:50. Those are the ones that can change a number a user sees (e.g. a returned note string containing "stub:", or a throw whose message says "not yet supported"). Classify-by-grep is not currently a test, so the 36 honest notes and the 2 live ones are indistinguishable to CI.
goals.acceptance: A test classifies every hit: comment-line hits must be recognised as scope notes, and every code-line hit must either be removed or be backed by a named, dated, honest-scope entry. The classification is asserted, not eyeballed. `node tests/test_stub_classification.js` (or the chosen filename) fails if a new code-line stub appears.

goals.title: The syntax gate checks 66 files under src/ and ZERO of the 15 .mjs files that run the loop itself
goals.thesis: evolve.mjs:runGate walks path.join(ROOT,"src") for *.js and scripts/check.sh does `find src -type f -name '*.js'` — both scoped to src/. The 15 non-src modules (evolve/evolve.mjs, scripts/calibration_4w52.mjs, scripts/fetch_coreset.mjs, scripts/pareto_bench.mjs, scripts/smoke_browsers.mjs, scripts/test_bindlog.mjs, ...) are never node --check'd by any gate, including evolve/evolve.mjs itself. The loop that gates the project is ungated: a syntax error in it makes the loop silently do nothing while CI stays green. Measured: 66 gated vs 15 ungated.
goals.acceptance: scripts/check.sh (and the gate's syntax component) covers every tracked .js/.mjs outside node_modules/ and tests/ — at minimum all of: evolve/evolve.mjs, scripts/calibration_4w52.mjs, scripts/fetch_coreset.mjs, scripts/pareto_bench.mjs. A planted syntax error in evolve/evolve.mjs makes `npm run check` exit non-zero.
